body:
Why does it feel wrong to you?

The name registered in `VARIANT_ENUM_CAST` / `VARIANT_ENUM_CAST_EXT` must match the one used by `BIND_ENUM_CONSTANT`, so it would be the safest to just re-use it. Not re-using it would be error prone.

With the approach I mentioned, it'd be re-used. The part that feels wrong to me is making every single enum value name in the codebase go through this :: slicing path when it's only needed for this specific exceptional case.

So is it a performance concern? That's fair, but I doubt it will have a noticeable impact, since it's only a few hundred strings created once during startup. I expect it will take a microsecond or so.
That, and I think using a separate macro makes it much more explicit instead of the implementation slicing :: under the hood. If that's fine, I'd like to go with the approach I mentioned earlier.

I don't like the possibility of someone using the `_EXT` macros and accidentally mismatching cast and bind, creating an incorrect state. Whatever state the cast sets up should be used by the binds.
Like you, I also don't like that it will mean additional work for the non-ext macros, but we might be able to address this differently in the future. But I think correctness / stability is more important than performance, especially if the actual performance impact is negligible.
Alright, I went with your initial suggestion.

I should note that before, it was using `Scope::Value`, now it's using `Value`. We could prepend the scope (via a second parameter), but depending on what exactly it's used for, it may not matter.
In the current implementation, how do the docs show the fully qualified enum name?

EnumType.EnumValue

This argument _always_ is the enum value in the codebase without any scopes, the sole exception being just the enums we modified. Since get_slice returns the string itself when :: is not found, the behavior stays the same for the regular cases.
